messages.content: 尋找兩家電影院，位於聖地牙哥附近，提供下午5點的《天能》和晚上7點半的《007生死交戰》場次。

function.name: find_movie_showing
function.description: Find local movie theatres and their schedule for a specific movie Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city and state, e.g. San Diego, CA

message.reasoning:
The user wants to find two movie theaters near San Diego that have showtimes: 5pm for "Tenet" (天能) and 7:30pm for "007生死交戰" (No Time To Die). We need to use the function find_movie_showing. The function signature expects location: string, movie: "Tenet" | "No Time To Die"[], time: string[]. So we need to call the function twice? Actually we need to find two theaters. The function returns any. We can call it twice with different times? But the function expects an array of times. We can pass both times? But the movie param is either Tenet or No Time To Die. We need separate calls: one for Tenet at 5pm, one for No Time To Die at 7:30pm. But the user wants two theaters that have both showtimes? Or two theaters: one for Tenet at 5pm, one for No Time To Die at 7:30pm. The phrasing: "尋找兩家電影院，位於聖地牙哥附近，提供下午5點的《天能》和晚上7點半的《007生死交戰》場次。" Means "Find two movie theaters near San Diego that offer 5pm showing of Tenet and 7:30pm showing of No Time To Die." It could mean find two theaters: one that has Tenet at 5pm, another that has No Time To Die at 7:30pm. So we need to call function twice.

We need to provide location: "San Diego, CA". For Tenet: movie: "Tenet", time: ["5:00 PM"]. For No Time To Die: movie: "No Time To Die", time: ["7:30 PM"].

We should call the function twice. Use the function name find_movie_showing. Provide arguments accordingly.
